requirements.summary: [Q2] Risk management: metrics as fields in Jira
requirements.description_excerpt: Before the change: Metrics from the Risk Management module only live in BigPicture, they cannot be mapped to any Jira field. Only Risk Probability and Risk Consequence from the old Risk module can be mapped to Jira fields. After the change: Metrics from the Risk Management module can be mapped to a Jira field, either created automatically by BigPicture (like Risk Probability and Risk Consequence) or user can select a Jira field to which they want to map those metrics. Best place to add it - as risk Register settings → Metrics

acceptance_criteria.text: In case multiple contexts - Risk matrix should display only default context for this first iteration.

A Jira field created automatically by BigPicture (Epic description)

Default field context only (AC field; Confluence weekly sync)

findings.excerpt_quote: In case multiple contexts - Risk matrix should display only default context for this first iteration.
findings.finding_summary: The Epic's only acceptance criterion covers the multiple-contexts edge case. The core outcome in "After the change" (a metric mapped to a Jira field, configured in Risk Register settings → Metrics) has no epic-level completion criterion; the detail lives in individual child descriptions only.
findings.testing_impact: Regression and sign-off can't be checked against one epic-level definition of done; QA has to rebuild it from ten child descriptions.
findings.question_for_PM: What epic-level acceptance criteria define the core mapping as delivered?

findings.excerpt_quote: either created automatically by BigPicture (like Risk Probability and Risk Consequence) or user can select a Jira field to which they want to map those metrics
findings.finding_summary: The Epic names two paths: a Jira field created automatically by BigPicture, and a user-selected field. Every child description with matching terms covers the user-selected path only (listing fields, a field dropdown, context options). No child description mentions creating a Jira field, and no source states that path was dropped or deferred.
findings.testing_impact: Regression scope for the automatic-field path can't be set: it is unknown whether it shipped, so it is neither tested nor explicitly excluded.
findings.question_for_PM: Was the automatically created Jira field path delivered, deferred, or dropped?

findings.excerpt_quote: Need to open the config if the values has been changed
findings.finding_summary: Elena Kolesnik's comment (2026-07-17) lists two items: reopening the configuration after values change, and adding the field to the screen so it is visible in Risk Management. There is no reply or linked follow-up. Both match behaviour in child descriptions (ONE-249893, ONE-320856, ONE-257569), but whether they were acted on, for example in the documentation request DOCBP-4395, isn't recorded.
findings.testing_impact: Sign-off can't confirm whether these two items are expected product behaviour to regress, or documentation notes only.

findings.excerpt_quote: This change needs to be synchronised to the issue entity property when listing the risk register issues table
findings.finding_summary: A value changed directly in the Jira field reaches BigPicture only when the risk register issues table is listed (ONE-320856). The listener story ONE-257529 was Canceled, and ONE-257576 states that recalculation covers only the listed issues, leaving the stored values outdated for the rest. The expected state of Risk Score and Risk Level for issues not yet listed, for example on the Risk matrix, is not stated.
findings.testing_impact: Regression can cover the listed-table sync, but not what other views should show before an issue is listed.

findings.excerpt_quote: If metric is linked to a custom field, then all issues in which have option selected for the metric, needs to update the custom field value in Jira
findings.finding_summary: ONE-320856 has the frontend update the Jira field for one issue on selection, and for every affected issue when a metric option changes in the configuration. No source states what happens when a Jira update fails or only some issues update.
findings.testing_impact: Failure and partial-update cases can't be given expected results.

findings.finding_summary: ONE-249893 asks who can change the metric configuration and which custom fields are listed. The answers are recorded only as images, which Epic mode does not read, and no child states a role rule in text.
findings.testing_impact: Role-based regression cases (who may link a field to a metric) can't be written from text sources.

findings.excerpt_quote: [MetricCustomFields][Frontend] Only list custom field options from the default context
findings.finding_summary: ONE-272341 implements the Epic's only acceptance criterion (default context only), and ONE-293797 covers configuration persistence, but both have an empty description (title only). Their alignment with the Epic rests on the title alone.
findings.testing_impact: The default-context and persistence regressions have no child-level expected result to check against.

findings.finding_summary: No source says how the feature reached users: no feature flag, staged rollout, or explicit release to everyone. The Confluence project page plans release 8.74 for frontend and backend, and the children's fix versions include hedgeppm-cloud-1.0.0 (released 2026-08-03) and bigpicture-cloud-8.74.0.2 (released 2026-07-30).
findings.testing_impact: Regression can't target the right audience or configuration without knowing whether the feature is on for everyone.

findings.excerpt_quote: Work completed; we can mark as completed after QA & Product acceptance
findings.finding_summary: The Epic is Done, but no testing child, QA acceptance record, or linked Xray execution was found on the Epic. The Confluence project page names a QA owner and makes QA and Product acceptance the completion step, with no record of either.
findings.testing_impact: Sign-off can't state what was verified, so regression scope has to start from nothing.

findings.finding_summary: No performance consideration is stated for updating every affected issue from the frontend when a metric option changes (ONE-320856), or for adding editmeta to the bulk issue fetch.
findings.testing_impact: No load expectation to check for large risk registers.

findings.finding_summary: No logging, audit, or changelog entry is mentioned for linking a metric to a Jira field or for the resulting Jira field updates.

report.readiness_line: 2 High findings (RR-ONE-181964-01, RR-ONE-181964-02) and 2 High questions (Q1, Q6) stand between this Epic and a complete regression and sign-off scope.

facts.text: Goal: metrics from the Risk Management module can be mapped to a Jira field, either created automatically by BigPicture or selected by the user, configured in Risk Register settings → Metrics.
Acceptance criterion: "In case multiple contexts - Risk matrix should display only default context for this first iteration."
Weekly sync decision: "We will not support multiple custom field contexts. Only default context will be used."
facts.source: Confluence — "Risk management: Link custom fields to metrics - Q2 26'" (appfireteam.atlassian.net)

facts.text: Planned scope: "We will list custom fields of type select"; "User will be allowed to select a color for each option"; "User will be allowed to select a numeric value for each option"; "By default no custom field is linked to a metric".
Owners named: Product Elena Kolesnik, UX Karolina Chrzanowska, Engineering Leo Nunes / Valter Junior / Przemysław Dziedzic, QA Chai Prasad K. Release 8.74 planned for both frontend and backend.
facts.source: Confluence — "Risk management: Link custom fields to metrics - Q2 26'" (appfireteam.atlassian.net)

facts.text: Selected metric values are stored in the Jira issue entity property and, for linked metrics, also in the Jira custom field. Jira-side changes are synced when the risk register issues table is listed.
Options added to or deleted from the Jira field appear on the configuration page and reach the select list once the configuration is saved.
Out of scope for this work: "Add/Remove more values when using Jira fields".
facts.source: ONE-249893 description, "Future requirements [Not on this task]"

facts.text: The listener for Jira-side field changes (ONE-257529, stretch goal) was Canceled with resolution Won't Do on 2026-06-16.

Screenshot 1 shows "RR - Settings" with a Metrics section: Likelihood (Rare to Certain, values 1 to 5) and Consequence (Insignificant to Severe, values 1 to 5). Screenshot 2 is a Confluence "Risks configuration" capture labelled "Old Risks mapping example".

Linked design and delivery issues: UX-378 "Risk management: columns as fields in Jira" (Done), HED-288 "Metrics can be synchronized with Jira fields (single select)" (Done), DOCBP-4395 "Risk management: Metrics as fields in Jira" (Done).

risks.text: Values can drift between Jira and BigPicture for issues that aren't re-listed, because the listener story was Canceled. This is the Epic's main data-integrity regression surface.
Bulk frontend updates of every affected issue on a configuration change have no stated failure handling.
If the automatically created field path was expected by customers (the strategy page lists field mapping as a Hedge need), its absence would surface as a support issue rather than in regression.

testing_focus.text: Round trip: select a metric option in BigPicture and confirm the Jira field; change the Jira field and confirm the risk register table, Risk Score, and Risk Level after listing.
Default-context-only behaviour and the two messages in ONE-326432 for fields without a default context or options.
Dropdown disabled states from editmeta, across team-managed and company-managed projects.
Changing or removing an option in the metric configuration and its effect on every affected issue.
Role coverage for linking a field to a metric.
Automatically created Jira field path, once its status is confirmed.
